🇷🇺⚔️🇺🇦 Ukrainian media: Will Russia strike Zelensky's office, the government and parliament?

After days of near round-the-clock attacks on Kiev, and today's hits in the city centre in particular, Ukrainian media are openly asking why one part of the capital has so far been left untouched: the government quarter.

Recent strikes have exposed how vulnerable Kiev is to Russian drones and ballistic missiles alike. Yet Zelensky's office, the government headquarters and Ukraine's parliament have not been targeted.

Russian Telegram channels have long asked why Moscow does not strike Kiev's "decision-making centres."

The explanations in Russian and Ukrainian channels floated over the years range from an unofficial agreement between the two governments, to strikes being pointless because Ukraine's leadership spends most of its time in Soviet-era bunkers built for Communist Party officials in case of nuclear war, to claims that attacks were attempted but everything was shot down by Kiev's air defence.

Ukrainian commentators now say that last explanation no longer holds, with drones and missiles hitting wherever they want in the capital. Government buildings are also far from empty, with events held there regularly and parliament still meeting at its official address.

The prevailing view in Ukrainian media is that unless there is some "shadow" moratorium on striking the central authorities of the warring states, the safety of Ukraine's top officials and MPs is now more pressing than at any point since the start of the war. A strike on the government quarter is moving from a theoretical threat to a very real one.

Talk of moving parliament sessions elsewhere, a full relocation of the government, and tighter security around Zelensky's movements is expected to intensify. Rumours are already circulating in Ukrainian Telegram channels that the Kiev regime is considering moving some government activities, including parliament, to Lvov.

As for why the quarter has been spared so far, two theories dominate: Moscow may be holding those targets in reserve as retaliation for a special case, such as Ukrainian missiles or drones reaching central Moscow. Or the strikes are already planned and Russia is waiting for the right moment.
